questions.q: Which threads can read or write any location in global memory?
options: Only threads within the same block
Only thread 0 of each block
Any thread, in any block, with no automatic coordination
Only threads with an even threadIdx.x
questions.explain: Global memory is visible to every thread in every block. There's no built-in restriction or coordination, so concurrent writes to the same location without synchronization cause a race condition.

questions.q: What is the scope of __shared__ memory declared inside a kernel?
options: A single thread
A single block — every thread in that block sees the same shared array
The entire grid across all blocks
It persists across multiple kernel launches
questions.explain: __shared__ memory is scoped to one block. Every thread within that block shares the same array, but a different block gets its own separate copy.

options: It terminates all threads in the block immediately
It forces every thread in a block to reach that line before any of them proceeds
It synchronizes the GPU clock with the CPU
It copies shared memory back to global memory automatically
questions.explain: __syncthreads() is a barrier: no thread in the block proceeds past it until every thread in the block has reached that point, which is essential when threads depend on each other's writes to shared memory.

questions.q: Despite its name, why is "local memory" in CUDA not actually fast?
options: Local memory is a marketing term with no real hardware backing
Local memory is private to a thread like a register, but it is physically stored in the same slow global memory space
Local memory is only accessible from the host CPU
Local memory is faster than shared memory but has less capacity
questions.explain: Local memory is per-thread in scope (like registers), but physically implemented using the same slow global memory space, used automatically by the compiler when registers run out.

questions.q: Which memory tier has the broadest scope (visible to the entire grid) but is also the slowest?
options: Register
Shared memory
Local memory
Global memory
questions.explain: Global memory is visible across the entire grid (all blocks, all threads) and persists until explicitly freed, but it is the slowest of the four tiers.
